key_insight: Representing depth as a neural implicit field with a local implicit decoder lets models predict continuous depth at any 2D coordinate, enabling arbitrary-resolution and fine-grained geometry recovery from images.
problem_solved: Overcomes the limitation of discrete image-grid depth outputs that cannot be queried at arbitrary resolutions or capture fine geometric detail.
method: Encode input image into multi-scale feature maps, then combine local image features with continuous 2D coordinates.
Use a local implicit decoder (coordinate-conditioned neural field) to regress depth values at continuous spatial queries, enabling arbitrary-resolution output.
Train the network end-to-end on paired image-depth data so the implicit field learns to reconstruct fine geometric detail when upsampling or zooming.
impact: Enables practitioners to produce high-resolution, geometry-preserving depth maps from standard image inputs without being tied to discrete pixel grids — useful for 3D reconstruction, AR/VR, and robotics. Facilitates scalable evaluation and deployment at multiple output resolutions.
visual_elements: Diagram: pipeline showing image encoder -> local implicit decoder + continuous (x,y) query -> depth value

paper_title: InfiniDepth: Arbitrary-Resolution and Fine-Grained Depth Estimation with Neural Implicit Fields
paper_authors: Hao Yu, Haotong Lin, Jiawei Wang, Jiaxin Li, Yida Wang
